note_tweet.text:
reality checks after reality checks
i simply feel inferior to cis female and cis male
the oestrogen i’m taking means nothing compared to natural female puberty. 
anyways, that’s no news to me. it just punches me in the face every time i socialise with all these “normal people”. 
i guess i’m just not supposed to be normal after all.
i was fine and all if i’ll never go outside and talk to people, but i feel detached and misaligned everywhere i go since hrt.
ever since i took the first tablet i knew i would not want to go back, but it’s that burning pain of the lost of identity and constantly being reminded of the misalignments that’s killing me form the inside.
why am i still “one of the boys” when i never wanted it in the first place. i admire the inclusivity of male communities, but i’m just that one exception. i could not blend into both of the binary gender groups socially; and please forgive me for saying this, but i don’t like to consider myself as non-binary; i would much prefer to be assumed male or female if i’m mostly passing.
i’ve actually thought about this for a bit. i simply don’t think I would consider myself enby if i’m passing; even though people think the male body sits well on my character, i am disgusted by it. so i think the common understanding is: i one were to look like whatever they may, what would they identify as, that’s why i gave that analogy and asked myself that question.
anyways 
i’m just tired of feeling both my body and my soul is proving myself wrong with who i claim myself to be.
it’s just the beginning isn’t it
